$description: Design tokens of the interface (docs-fr/design/03-systeme.md). Format: W3C Design Tokens Community Group draft ($value, $type, $description). tools/design/tokens.mjs checks every contrast and colour-vision distance and writes docs-fr/design/maquettes/tokens.css. Values chosen by measure, 12/10/2026.

map.$description: Map and PAR background, the 'None (black)' base map.

panel.$description: Panels: list, radio bar, aircraft card, settings; unchanged.

raised.$description: Popovers, menus, help bubbles, chips on a panel.

hover.$description: Hover of a row or control; the darkest surface every text token must pass on.

selected.$description: Selected row, active tab, active filter: opaque green, so text contrast does not depend on what lies behind.

urgent.$description: Background of an emergency line in the journal or the list.

secondary.$description: Labels, types, secondary values. 7.2:1 on hover.

tertiary.$description: Units, timestamps, hints. 4.7:1 on hover: the floor.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls only (exempt from WCAG contrast).

on-accent.$description: Text on a filled accent button.

default.$description: Panel edges, the main separator; unchanged.

control.$description: Outline of an input, an unchecked box, an off toggle: at least 3:1 on panel, raised and hover (WCAG 1.4.11).

default.$description: The tool's voice: brand, live, selected, focus. One green only (the #4ADE80 of the sign-in page goes).

strong.$description: Accent text on the selected surface when more weight is needed (8.1:1 on panel).

urgent.$description: Emergency and failure, as text or icon; always with a shape or word.

urgent-fill.$description: Emergency badge (white text 6.5:1), always outlined with status.urgent (6.4:1 on panel), which detaches it from the panel. Darker than the accent so that a deuteranope tells them apart by lightness (ΔE 18).

warn.$description: Attention: degraded service, weak match, go-around, runway change.

info.$description: Neutral information that is not the tool's voice: help marker, link.

ok.$description: Status light 'ok' = the accent: a working chain is a live chain.

unknown.$description: Status light 'unknown' = tertiary text, hollow shape.

phase.$description: Five families instead of ten colours, the code (T/O, CLB…) always written beside. Minimal ΔE between families under normal sight and the three dichromacies: 23.8 (was 1.8).

cruise.$description: CRZ. Pale sky: high and passing.

arrival.$description: ARR, APP, T/D. Blue: coming in.

unknown.$description: NEW, UNK. Grey: nothing known yet.

altitude.$description: Aircraft icon on the map, by altitude band: a ramp of hue from warm and bright near the ground to cool and quiet at cruise (palette F, chosen by the owner on 13/10 after the grey ramp was refused in use: too hard to tell apart). Every pair of bands stays apart under the four visions, none looks like the urgent red, none like a phase family; near the ground = most visible, cruise = least (tools/design/altitude.mjs).

very-low.$description: Very low, near the ground: pale yellow, the most visible.

cruise.$description: Cruise: slate, the quietest: the most numerous and the least relevant to a local listener.

very-low.$description: Very low on a light base map (IGN, OSM): dark olive, the most visible.

map.$description: The map's own layers, palette C chosen by the owner on 15/10: the hues of the map are kept (aerodromes and VOR blue, VORTAC indigo, NDB amber, small aerodromes, heliports and DME violet) and only what clashed with a colour that means something is changed: the selection and the followed track take the accent instead of a yellow that read as a very low aircraft, taxiways and range rings go grey, an aircraft's trail takes its altitude colour, estimates (future, hindcast) are the accent dotted. Colours the map draws on its own, read from these tokens.

airport.$description: Large and medium airports, symbol and code (medium ones were #34D399, a green dE76 2.2 from the ground phase at worst, and the accent's family).

airport-small.$description: Small aerodromes and seaplane bases (these were #2DD4BF, dE76 3.4 from a low aircraft at worst).

heliport.$description: Heliport symbol and code: violet, with the small aerodromes; it was #FB923C, dE76 3.3 from the departure phase at worst.

centerline.$description: Extended runway centrelines, dashed: grey, were #76C76C, dE76 1.2 from the accent; they cross the whole map.

taxiway.$description: Taxiway: grey, was pale yellow (#efe3a0), dE76 6.6 from a very low aircraft at worst.

ring.$description: Range rings: grey, were the accent.

ring-label.$description: Range ring labels ("10 NM"): the tertiary text.

selected.$description: Ring of the selected aircraft, 2 px: the accent, was #FDE047.

hovered.$description: Ring of the hovered aircraft, 1.2 px: primary text, was #86EFAC.

trail-followed.$description: Track of the followed aircraft, dashed. Other aircraft's trails take their altitude colour at 50 %.

estimate.$description: Estimated positions, dotted: the future and the hindcast (were #FFC107 and #00BCD4).

trail-stale.$description: Trail of an aircraft whose position is getting old or lost: tertiary, as the lost glyph.

procedure.$description: A published route (SID, STAR) and its named points: a reference, neutral, not the aircraft's track (its altitude colour, or the accent when followed). Full for the route asked for, at 38 % in the Procedures layer.

proximity.$description: The Nearby tab's circle around the followed aircraft, dashed, fill at 6 %: it belongs to the followed flight; was #EB8C00, dE76 0.9 from the departure phase.

ring.$description: Range rings on a light base map (IGN, OSM).

centerline.$description: Extended centrelines on a light base map.

proximity.$description: The Nearby circle on a light base map.

procedure.$description: A published route on a light base map.

taxiway.$description: Taxiway on a light base map.

selected.$description: Selection ring on a light base map (4.5:1 on the OSM ground).

hovered.$description: Hover ring on a light base map.

trail-stale.$description: Old or lost trail on a light base map.

ground.$description: Ground of a chip over a light base map (the altitude legend).

scrim.$description: Behind a full page (settings) over the map: black at 70 %.

mono.$value: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace
mono.$description: What is compared: callsigns, frequencies, levels, headings, speeds, times, codes.

text.$description: What is read: transcriptions, plain-language instructions, help, messages. Local fonts only.

caption.$description: Floor. Units, field labels (upper case), timestamps, badges.

small.$description: Dense data: table cells, secondary lines of a row.

display.$description: Page title, the one big number of a card.

space.$description: 2 px steps up to 8, then 4 px steps: 2, 4, 6, 8 cover 77 % of today's uses.

lg.$description: Panels floating over the map, popovers.

strong.$description: Focus ring, selected aircraft, active tab underline.

overlay.$description: Only for what floats over the map (popover, help bubble), where the base map may be bright. Nothing else casts a shadow: on black it does not show.

alert-pulse.$description: Emergency only: three pulses, then steady.

target-desk.$description: Minimal side of a pointer target on the desk.

target-touch.$description: Minimal side of a touch target on the phone.

row-desk.$description: Aircraft row in the list, desk: two lines (body 20 + caption 14) and 2 x 4 px padding, plus 2 px gap. Today about 50 px (12/10 captures).

row-touch.$description: Aircraft row in the list, phone: the whole row is the target.

control-desk.$description: Height of a button, toggle or segment on the desk.

control-touch.$description: Height of a control on the phone.

control-large.$description: A control that carries two texts: the search field, a channel button.

panel-head.$description: Header of a panel (title and quiet actions).

tabs-head.$description: Header of the context column: its two tabs and the fold button.

bar.$description: The top bar: the sign, what is on air, the lights, the clock.
